Is something like this what you had in mind?

library('ggplot2')

# Generate a faux data set with which to work
DF <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(1:2, each = 100)),
x = rnorm(200),
y = rnorm(200))

# Set the alpha transparency level in geom_point()
# rather than in scale_manual()
ggplot(DF, aes(x, y, colour = gp)) +
geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
theme_bw() +
scale_colour_manual(values = c('blue', 'orange')) +
guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))

The last line uses the guides functions new to version 0.9.0; this
particular call will put the fully saturated colors in the legend but
the plotted points will have the defined level of transparency.

HTH,
Dennis

Hi:

This might be a little easier and require only a single legend:

ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=gp2),size=7,
position=position_jitter(width=0.95,height=1.1),
alpha = 0.2) +
scale_shape_manual(values = c(0, 1, 15, 16)) +
guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))

Shapes can be filled or unfilled; see the table on p.197 of the
ggplot2 book. In this case, 0 = unfilled square, 1 = unfilled circle
and 15 and 16 are their filled counterparts, respectively. You can
always use the labels = argument of scale_shape_manual() to label them
appropriately.

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
Hi.

I've had this problem before and thought I had solved it but now it returns.  The problem is that the geom_segment and geom_text call cause overplotting of lines and text and it is blurry.  Maybe I have just lost the concept of what is going on but I cannot figure out why these simple functions should interact in a way that causes this degradation in plot quality.

p2 + geom_point(size=3) +
     geom_segment(data=NULL, xend=33.80, x=34.8, yend= -0.3, y = 0.0, show_guide=F, linetype=2, color="black") +
     geom_segment(xend= 5.00, x=34.8, yend=-17.0, y = 0.0, show_guide=F, linetype=2, color="red") +
     geom_segment(xend=34.42, x=34.8, yend= -0.3, y = 0.0, show_guide=F, linetype=1, color="blue") +
     xlim(min(C$Salinity),max(C$Salinity)) + ylim(min(C$dO18),max(C$dO18)) +
     ylab(expression(paste(delta,{}^18*"O ("^o*"/"[oo]*")"))) + xlab('Salinity (psu)') +
     geom_text(x=34.47,y=-0.08,label="Upper Circumpolar Deep Water -->", color="black", angle=37, size = 3) +
     geom_text(x=34.09,y=-0.44,label="<-- Iceberg fragment \n dO18 = -17, Salinity = 5.0", angle=57, size = 3, color="red") + 
     geom_text(x=34.53,y=-0.25,label="Ambient", angle=65, size = 3, color="blue") +   
     geom_text(x=34.20,y=-0.25, label="<--- Melting   Freezing --->", size = 3, color = "black") + 
     stat_smooth(method="loess") +
     scale_colour_manual("Site",values=c("C18A"="black","Far-field"="magenta"))

Can someone tell me why this is happening?  I cannot figure out why the overplotting occurs in the text and the dashed lines.

Hi John,

I'm surprised that works at all. I didn't know you could specify x and
y outside of an aes call.

Anyway, I think you are looking for ?annotate. For example, replace

geom_text(x=34.47,y=-0.08,label="Upper Circumpolar Deep Water -->",
color="black", angle=37, size = 3)

with

annotate("text", x=34.47,y=-0.08,label="Upper Circumpolar Deep Water
-->", color="black", angle=37, size = 3)

Hope that helps,
Ista

On Jun 15, 2012, at 9:31 AM, Ista Zahn wrote:

Hey John,

This looks pretty good to me (xlim commented out because you didn't
send the object C):

p2 = ggplot(E, aes(Salinity, dO18, color=Site))
p2 + geom_point(size=3) +
annotate("segment", x=34.8, xend=33.80, y=0.0, yend= -0.3,
linestyle=2, colour="black") +
annotate("segment", xend= 5.00, x=34.8, yend=-17.0, y = 0.0,
show_guide=F, linetype=2, color="red") +
annotate("segment", xend=34.42, x=34.8, yend= -0.3, y = 0.0,
show_guide=F, linetype=1, color="blue") +
#xlim(min(C$Salinity),max(C$Salinity)) + ylim(min(C$dO18),max(C$dO18)) +
ylab(expression(paste(delta,{}^18*"O ("^o*"/"[oo]*")"))) +
xlab('Salinity (psu)') +
annotate("text",x=34.47,y=-0.08,label="Upper Circumpolar Deep
Water -->", color="black", angle=37, size = 3) +
annotate("text",x=34.09,y=-0.44,label="<-- Iceberg fragment
dO18 = -17, Salinity = 5.0", angle=57, size = 3, color="red") +
annotate("text",x=34.53,y=-0.25,label="Ambient", angle=65, size =
3, color="blue") +
annotate("text",x=34.20,y=-0.25, label="<--- Melting Freezing
--->", size = 3, color = "black") +
stat_smooth(method="loess") +
scale_colour_manual("Site",values=c("C18A"="black","Far-field"="magenta"))

Does this do what you want? If not, can you be more specific about the problem?

Best,
Ista
